body: We booked a mahoora tented camp in Udawalawe as part of a road trip we did in April. The booking, which was very reasonably priced, came with a tour of the Udawalawe National Park. So, this visit wasn't planned and we had no expectations .... but everything just turned out to be a perfect experience!!!Udawalawe is the seventh largest national park in Sri Lanka and is mainly known for its elephant sightings. But we heard from our guide that on extremely rare occasions there has been sightings of leopards on evening tours. We chose the morning tour. Started from the camp at 6 am and arrived at the entrance to the park by 6.30 am. [We were told the best time to see the animals is either early morning or late evening. The park opens at 6 am but I am not sure of the closing time.] While there were some vehicles, it wasn't crowded. So, that's another plus about going as early as possible. [Also it's best to avoid local school holidays and long weekends.]Heavy rains had started two days prior (which was unusual for the region though) so we didn't have much expectations of seeing any animals. [We were also told the best time to visit the park was in the dry season from July - August where large herds of elephants would converge near the reservoir.]But to our surprise we saw around 10 elephants within 100 meters from the park entrance. Thereafter, there was a bit of a dry spell with no sightings except for birds and it started raining. But nevertheless we enjoyed the ride with our guide enthusiastically pointing out various birds. [While we did get a bit wet, the weather was cool and pleasant whereas a visit in the dry season would have been hot and dusty.] Then we met another herds of elephants with two baby elephants entertaining us with their antics. We stopped for a packed breakfast halfway through and all in all spent about 3 hours in the park. While park visits can always be a hit or miss, this experience turned out to be perfect. A lot of the credit should go to the echo team of the mahoora camp for their perfect organising. [I have written a separate review on our experience there.] They were so punctual, our driver was safe and reliable, our guide was knowledgeable and enthusiastic, the breakfast was lovely and the list goes on....While you can always book a vehicle at the park entrance, it would always be better to book a vehicle in advance ( or even through a hotel, though that might include a mark up) to ensure that you avoid crowds and arrive at a time more likely to result in elephants sightings. It must also be mentioned that compared to some time back, the safari jeeps were also in relatively good condition both in terms of emissions and safety. Udawalawe National park also offers a free tusker sighting ;) The fellow is christened "Bullet" and can be found at the electric fence running parallel to the main road a little way after the park entrance (if you are coming from Udawalawe junction side) throughout the day and almost all year around. While the locals may urge you to feed him (and while that's why he is standing there) it's best not to do so for his own good health.Udawalawe National Park also has an Elephant Orphanage and unlike Pinnawala, they release the baby elephants back into the wild after rehabilitation. You can pay a fee and see them being fed with milk. There is one session in the morning (not sure of the timing) and one at 2.30 pm. The entrance to this place is on a turn - off a little before the park entrance when coming from the Udawalawe junction. We went for a session in July of last year. While they do good work there (there is a also a programme to adopt/ sponsor a baby elephant) i had rather ambivalent feelings about the viewing experience of the feeding (those who know would know;) hence opted not to review that particular experience....

body: I visited Udawalawe National Park, Hurulu Eco Park and Yala National Park and enjoyed Udawalawe the most.In general, I think the local authorities need to do something about overselling the tours in their parks, as the numbers of safari cars in the last two parks were insane. I have never seen so many jeeps on any given day in any of the countless safaris I’ve had all over Africa.Some sightings of elephants we had in Hurulu or one sighting of leopards in Yala were accompanied by dozens and dozens of jeeps, making it nearly impossible for us to even get a glimpse of the animals.This is the reason why I enjoyed Udawalawe the most. It is less visited, but has the same animals we saw in Yala National park, so observing the wildlife without too many other jeeps was way more enjoyable. I would recommend Sri Lanka for the bird watching more than for the animals. The amount of birds I was able to see and record was incredible.I organized a private 7-hour tour of Udawalawe park through Lahiru. His whatsapp number is ‪+94 76 272 6799‬. I contacted several providers and his price was very competitive. He arranged a very comfy van transport for me from Hikkaduwa beach at the most affordable price on a less than 12-hour notice. I made a very last minute booking.Lahiru is very attentive, thoughtful and is a very knowledgeable guide. He showed me every bird we saw in the book he had and had a lot of information about the flora and fauna of the park.I highly recommend him.
title: Great 7-hour safari of the park with a fantastic guide

body: I had the most amazing experience at udawalawe national park with Lahiru as my guide. Lahiru is so knowledgeable about elephants and other wildlife in the park. He spots things that you would have never seen yourself! Visiting the udawalawe national park was the absolute highlight of my trip. We saw around 20 elephants - some males on their own but mainly herds of females with their babies which was so lovely to see!The next day we also went to the elephant orphanage which is part of the national park. The babies who have lost their mums are looked after here until they are ready to go back into the main part of the national park / wild and you get to see them being fed. I absolutely love elephants so I went to another national park during my trip but it just did not compare to this day! Would highly recommend udawalawe with Lahiru as your guide - it’s just so lovely seeing the elephants in their natural habitat and it is not crowded with jeeps because the national park is so big and Lahiru made an effort to go different routes to other jeeps and was so respectful of the elephants! Not only did I have the best couple of days seeing the elephants, but Lahiru also helped me with my accommodation in Udawalawe, transport for the rest of my trip and recommendations of where to visit. Thank you for all your help Lahiru and for making my trip to udawalawe national park so special!

body: We had a wonderful guide Lahiru who surprised us a lot with his knowledge of the park itself and the animals within it. There isn’t a question he couldn’t answer and throughout the 4 hour drive we had every single species we saw was easily recognised and described by him. The park itself is a true testament to nature and although there is a bit more tourist activity here it doesn’t spoil the atmosphere and vibe of the place. The park itself is hard to comprehend in its size since we’d only seen about 5% of it but the animals ( and our guide descriptions ) were top notch. I don’t think I’ve ever seen a couple week old elephant up close before ( AND ITS ALSO IN THE WILD ). No luck on leopards tho but it makes sense since they mostly come out to hunt in the morning and we finished our trip at 18. In total we saw 23 different bird species( including colourful bee eaters peacocks parrots toucans and not so colourful kites and eagle-hawks) a monitor lizard a Marsh crocodile, about 30-40 elephants, some deer and of course buffalos. I’d recommend the trip even if you think that the safari will bore you ( as I thought ) and I was genuinely surprised by how much fun we had. Here is a number for our guide ( +94762726799 )and I wish you all good luck in spotting animals.

body: The park is great but here are some thoughts:You will see elephants. But you have to be observant/lucky to see a lot else: deer are likely, mongooses, monitors, wild boar, jackal, crocs passably likely. There's a good number of birds. The peacocks are amazing.One minus is the price at $35 pp. ....for which you get hopelessly rutted tracks and far too much traffic, noisy diesel engines. on top of the $35 you have to hire your jeep at, say, $20 for 3 hours, and a further few dollars if you want a spotter too ...don't expect witty repartee. For the most part, you have the thing you are seeing named ...and not much else. We had a better afternoon trip for sightings than we did by getting up for a 6.30 start (although fewer ellies)There doesn't seem to be much etiquette amongst the jeeps - either towards the animals or towards other jeeps. The elephants seem to be remarkably chilled about it. Udawalawe is good, but it doesn't compare to an african safari. One or two half day visits are more than enough unless you have a bird interest (in which case you'd need to find a better than average guide)
title: Good trip, but there are buts...

body: Well we chose this national park over the others as we were advised it was more respectful of the animals and less crowded. We paid for the safari with our stay at the River camp. When we arrived we were told we needed to pay the entrance fee - approximately $30 per person on top - so basically paid for an expensive driver in a jeep - not sure if there is a cheaper way to do it - like book without safari and then negotiate when you get there? Anyway - a guide would have also cost more on top so we declined as we know a lot about the animals already. As we came into the park, we were effectively following in convoy and we were shocked that so many people were in their own jeeps - some people literally on their own. This made us feel quite uncomfortable, as we would have preferred the option to share a jeep for a lesser price so that there were not so many diesel spewing engines around the animals and noise. It took quite awhile to find anything at first- then the drivers would let each other know and there would be a bit of a ‘traffic jam’ for a bit, which we didn’t like. body: dawalawe National Park is a national park on the boundary of Sabaragamuwa and Uva Provinces in Sri Lanka. The park was created to provide a sanctuary for wild animals displaced by the construction of the Udawalawe Reservoir on the Walawe River, as well as to protect the catchment of the reservoir. The reserve covers 30,821 hectares (119.00 sq mi) of land area and was established on 30 June 1972.[1]Before the designation of the national park, the area was used for shifting cultivation (chena farming). The farmers were gradually removed once the national park was declared. The park is 165 kilometres (103 mi) from Colombo. Udawalawe is an important habitat for water birds and Sri Lankan elephants. It is a popular tourist destination and the third-most visited park in the country.[2]

body: We had an incredible time in Udawalawe – in large part because we booked with the incredible Mansala Safari Resort. Whether staying in their beautiful hotel or just taking their safari, we can’t recommend them enough – they’re one of the best choices I’ve made while travelling.Mansala basically arrange everything – safari, binoculars, transit, entry to the national park – and you pay at the end. It was one of the cheapest options we found but also one of the best.Tiron’s guide Tharanga took us on our safari. Like Tiron, he’s locally born and a genuine animal lover. He did everything the guidebooks tell you you’ll want in a guide – he was respectful of the animals, never crowded them, avoided hotspots full of other drivers, gave us information without overloading us, and showed us everything. We saw:- A herd of baby elephants- Crocodiles- Water buffalo- Lots of deer, including stags and, essentially, bambi- A family of wild boar, including 8 gorgeous little piglets running about in what my partner called ‘the best thing I’ve ever seen’- Lots of birds, including peacocks, storks, different types of eagles, woodsand pipers, little green bee eaters (really beautiful), cormorants, lapwings, hoopoes- A surprise tortoise- Surprise mongeeseYou can do an evening or morning safari, or both. We did an evening safari, which finishes before 6pm; we arrived at 2pm and went straight out onto it, which was more than enough time.The hotel itself is a lovely family-run operation, with two rooms and the family living in the building. Despite the homey, personal feel, everything from the food to the rooms to the safari is of the highest possible standard.Food is cooked by the family, eaten on the veranda with animals around – and is some of the best we ate on our trip. Eat there rather than going out into Udawalawe.The room was one of the best we stayed in in Sri Lanka, despite often paying significantly more than at Mansala – beautiful, comfortable, well-equipped, modern – everything we needed. Tiron, who runs the place, is a really kind and generous man. He was born in the house you’re staying in, knows the local area really well, and was one of our favourite people we met in Sri Lanka. When the driver he’d booked for our 2-hour drive to Mirissa was suddenly unavailable, he took us himself. His number is +94 77 795 9090 - he's given us permission to share it, and is very responsive to WhatsApps.If you want a really ethical, personal, kind experience, we can’t recommend Tiron, Tharanga and Mansala enough. We had a really special time, with really special people.

body: This park really needs to change the way they do safaris and limit the amount of vehicles in the park. The problem is that they allow hotels to arrange safaris--which all compete with each, this results in an abundance of vehicles in the park with only 1-2 people. So when you see a family of elephants, too many vehicles swarm around them, prohibiting the animals from moving in the direction they want, and causing them to be stressed. Furthermore, with so many vehicles in one area, the exhaust smell is strong and the engines are loud---also not good for the elephants. The park also needs to be stricter with the drivers by reminding them to keep distance and respect the animals.We all found this experience to be very troubling. I highly suggest when you book your safari, try booking through the park itself, and ask to be put with others in vehicles to limit them in the park. These animals need to be respected in their living space.

body: We took a 3 hr Safari booked through Viator with Bentota Travel. Bentota Travel is another story so i'm not going to say anything about that. We arrived at the reserve after going to the elephant sanctuary and transferred to a Jeep. Access to the jeep required climbing in through a narrow gap at the back of the vehicle while standing on a Beer crate!!! Not easy for a couple of portly nearly 60 year olds, but it makes for a good story afterwards!!We engaged the services of a guide ( they do not charge as such, you just tip them at the end of the safari what you think their services were worth) I would thoroughly recommend getting a guide. We didn't know where to look and the driver is too busy keeping his eye on the track to spot for you. In the end it was so worth having him as he was able to point out Monitors, Lizards, and birds that we just wouldn't have spotted. We saw wild buffalo, jackals, numerous colourful birds and birds of prey, Turtles, Lizards, Monitors and Loads of Elephants. We were lucky enough to see a family group of about 10 elephants along with 2 week old calf, a couple of smaller family groups, numerous single elephants (Including one asleep leaning against a tree!), but the highlight was a Mother and Calf pair who crossed the track in front of us and went to the lake edge to drink. They then proceeded to bathe and play in the water. At the same time, they were surrounded by buffalo complete with storks standing on their backs (I kid you not!!)All in all, an amazing 3 hrs and some of it quite emotional. We didn't seem to drive for more than a couple of minutes without seeing something. We did however meet some Landrovers with tourists and guide who had been in the park for 2 hrs and hadn't seen anything more than a couple of birds. i think we were extremely lucky and we happened to drop on a good guide who knew his stuff. Amazing Experience.P.s. Getting out of the Jeep was much easier, I went out through the front Drivers window!!!!
title: Awesome Safari

body: We took a three hour safari arranged by our hotel. We were very fortunate to see over thirty elephants around the tracks that we took. The safari cost is around $40 USD plus the entrance fee of $25USD for each person. Money taken in helps run the facility so great value. The more elephants protected the better. There are over three hundred elephants in this park. Don’t forget to tip your guide and driver - about 1000 rupees each.

body: I booked myself & partner in for an 8 hour tour of Udawalawe which we visited today, we choose Lahiru Prasad as our guide on a friends recommendation & TA reviews & booked him via Whatsapp (+94 76 272 6799). The National Park itself has amazing scenery, lagoons, bush & jungle along with lots of wildlife. We saw many different bird species including hawk, horn bills, fish owl, hummingbird, bee-eaters & jungle fowl, along with crocodiles, spotted deer, chameleons, mongoose, monitor lizards, wild boar and a pack of the rarely spotted golden jackal! We also saw 30 Elephants, solo males & herds of females along with 2 babies, one of which was only 2 months old. Most of our elephant spottings were just us alone with no other jeeps around, we were able to sit with a herd of females & baby eating grass around the jeep for over half an hour! Without sounding like an advert this was 100% down to Lahiru, he knows the park very well & took us on different trails to find the animals that other jeeps weren’t on. He’s super knowledgeable about all the animals & answered any questions we had & managed to spot animals other jeeps with just a driver were driving past & missing. As it is also mating season the male elephants were quite difficult to approach, despite this we felt very safe & confident in Lahiru‘s Jeep. Over the 8 hours Lahiru was still stopping & showing us things until we left the park, being so close to the elephants was an unforgettable experience, thank you Lahiru & driver & Udawalawe National Park! Lahiru also took us for a proper local curry afterwards & organised a very well priced taxi on to Ella for us!

body: Before our first holidays in Sri Lanka we tried to get some information and tipps about a game drive in the Udawalawe National Park. One name appeared again and again with only very excited positive reviews: Lahiru (Whatsapp +94 76 272 6799). We contacted him about 2 weeks before our trip and booked a Safari (1/2 day). We were very curious - is there a difference to other guides? Well, the first difference was: he even helped us to organize a driver who picked us up in after our train-journey in Ella and brought us to Udawalawe, which was very herpful. Yesterday we had our Safari with Lahiru. He picked us up at the hotel at 2 p.m. and then ... the whole afternoon was just AWESOME and OVERWHELMING!!! Lahiru is a very good Jeep-driver who really knows the park and all it's hidden paths. Most of the time we didn't see any other safari-jeeps (while many others were driving in small convoys on the "main roads") ... but therefore more animals than we expected to see! Elephants - of course (once we were lucky to stop close to some elephants an after some minutes we found ourselfs in the middle of a herd - and buffalos, deers, some crocodiles, gold-jackals, mungos, 3 differend types of eagles, ... and lots of birds (pelicans, toucans, bee-eaters, peacocks, ...) and even the fresh trace of a leopard. It was ... NO WORDS! Lahiru knows a lot about all these animals, his eyes seem to see everything while he is driving - it was perfect. He can also name some of the animals in German. I can recommend him as safari-guide without any doubt!And don't forget to visit the elephant-orphanage. They take care about orphants from outside the national park and set them free in the park when they are grown up. You can watch the feeding - cued! Very affordable and definitely worth it!

Our guide was very informative and pointed out things we would have easily missed, they are incredibly professional and well informed, not to mention exceptional drivers! Within minutes we were in the company of a majestic bull elephant who seemed quite undeterred by our proximity! We booked a couple of hours in the park, enough time to get up close and personal with the famous residents, including deer, water buffalo and a vast array of birds, lizards and mongoose, perhaps a longer tour might have increased our chances of seeing more than the 5 or 6 elephant we did, but by then we'd been bounced around enough! This is well worth the fee and advisable early start, if just to be that close to these magnificent creatures.

body: I had the most fantastic day with Chaminda, and recommend him wholeheartedly. He is polite, professional, sensitive to travellers’ needs and speaks pretty good English. He knows the names of all the animals in English and has reference books in the jeep. Most importantly he is knowledgeable about the creatures in the park and has a very good eye for spotting all manner of birds, mammals, and lizards. You can call him directly on his mobile +94 (077) 337 9470Chaminda charged me the standard rate for each half day game drive (currently 5,000 rupees) and freely gave me extra time on the morning drive in order to arrive early and beat the long queues, and then added more free extra time at the end too, as he was trying to find a brown fish owl. He spotted so many rare birds for me, and the brown fish owl eluded us on this trip! The afternoons are best for elephants as it’s too hot for birds until late afternoon, when visitors have to exit the park. title: Great park
body: This is a great national park. After visiting Yala national park, this is undoubtedly worlds better. The park is beautiful and so large that all the safari jeeps disperse nicely and it feels like a very private safari. The scenery is gorgeous with the mountain backdrop. The animals we saw very close by are fantastic. And our tour guide Janidth was the best (from Lakpura Solutions).

title: Baby elephants
body: We did a morning trip and this is a very well organised trip with many companies- perhaps too many as most of the vehicles had 1 or 2 people in , this is nice as you get plenty of space but not good for the environment as you could easily reduce the Impact to both the park and reduce the pollution . Nether the less this place is definitely worth a visit with plenty of wildlife about . We were lucky enough to see a croc ( briefly) , plenty of birds , elephants galore , a mongoose , spiky tortoise , jackals and a curious monkey . Seeing a 2 week old elephant with its mum and 5 yr old sister at a watering hole was the highlight of our holiday ! And our guide was very informative- although he could have spent less time on his mobile and shaking his legs whilst we took pics - also it would have shown more respect to the wildlife. There is not much else in the local area so 1 night stay on plenty .
